summary: Closed the two remaining Greptile security-review findings: plaintext bearer token over a non-loopback MCP HTTP bind, and every remaining code path or hint text advertising auth set-token as a positional argument.
reason: Round 1 fixed the unauthenticated MCP HTTP surface and the snapshot-label collision, and added a stdin option for auth set-token while keeping the positional form for backward compatibility. Greptile's round-2 re-review (score 1/5) confirmed the snapshot fix but flagged two remaining gaps: (1) the MCP HTTP transport defaults to loopback and requires a bearer token, but an operator overriding --addr to a non-loopback host still sends that token in plaintext with no transport encryption; (2) auth set-token still accepted and advertised a positional token argument in several places (auth.go's Use string, and hint text in helpers.go, client.go, and mcp/tools.go), which keeps the shell-history exposure vector alive regardless of the safer stdin alternative existing alongside it. Fixed by requiring WEAVIATE_COLLECTIONS_MCP_TLS_CERT/_KEY (and switching to ListenAndServeTLS) whenever the MCP HTTP bind address is not loopback, and by removing the positional-argument code path from auth set-token entirely (Args: cobra.NoArgs) plus purging every remaining hint string that showed the token as a CLI argument.
validated_outcome: Confirmed: `auth set-token abc123` now fails with a clear usage error (stdin only); `--transport http --addr 0.0.0.0:...` without TLS env vars refuses to start; `--transport http` on the loopback default with a token set still starts and correctly returns 401 for unauthenticated requests, 404 (reaches the handler) for authenticated ones. go build/vet clean; existing (pre-existing, unrelated) test failure confirmed present on the unmodified base commit too.
